clue.text: Athlete's tip for training — he knows what you are thinking

definitions.text: he knows what you are thinking

indicators.note: something put through training is worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports star passes on advice to someone who seems to read minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepathist claims to read minds directly, so such a person knows your thoughts without being told.

clue.text: Show some rare vitality

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An encouragement to display a little uncommon energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb but is a noun: a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is a Lloyd Webber stage musical, an example of a show.

clue.text: Oriental festival before 1st of November

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An Asian celebration falling before the start of November.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern and Oriental are synonyms describing the East.

clue.text: Cut top off piece of embroidery, it's more than enough!

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a sampler is a piece of embroidery showing stitches

explanation.surface: A needleworker trims an embroidery and declares it plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampler means more plentiful, more than enough.

clue.text: Managed in a huge complex producing slate

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone managed a giant building project that produced roofing stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like roofing stone; it is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to attack verbally, as does a long angry speech or rant at someone.

clue.text: Race official's second raised blast arresting you and I

indicators.note: in a down clue raised reads the piece upwards
arresting means holding inside

parts.note: drat and blast are both mild curses
together you and I are we

explanation.surface: A racing official shouts a curse at the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole container, not just the curse, so the result reads TEWARD after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards supervise race meetings and enforce the rules, especially in horse racing.

clue.text: Hire pro to broadcast about unravelling clue — him?

definitions.text: Hire pro to broadcast about unravelling clue — him?

indicators.note: one set of letters goes around the other
broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are scattered
something unravelled is untangled and reformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bring in a professional who will work out the riddle: is he the detective?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns HIRE PRO TO into HERPOIROT, which goes 'about' CULE, the letters 'unravelling' makes from 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective is the professional one hires to solve a mystery.

clue.text: Fawlty towers above art gallery and church

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece standing over another comes first

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: A hotel looms over an art gallery and a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawlty towers' recalls the sitcom title; here 'towers above' just places BASIL above ICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often with special privileges from the Pope.

clue.text: Entire prison's broken out, scattering

indicators.note: letters broken out of their order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whole jail has escaped, prisoners spreading everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersing things here and there among others is a scattering.

clue.text: European movies, long ones

parts.note: pics is informal for films, as in motion pictures

explanation.surface: Films from Europe that run for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long ones' refers back to movies: the definition leans on the wordplay's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Epics are lengthy, grand-scale films, so they are long movies.

clue.text: China's police ran amok

indicators.note: running amok is going wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The police force of China went on a rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but lower-case it is fine crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine ceramic tableware is called china, and that material is the same thing.

clue.text: Adaptable creature, desert animal accepting hard time

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: the camel is the classic animal of the desert
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A creature that copes with anything, a desert beast enduring a tough spell.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard changes its skin colour to suit its surroundings, the model of an adaptable animal.

clue.text: Emerge with a pay increase

parts.note: a rise is the British word for a salary increase

explanation.surface: Coming out of something with a better salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up or into view, as a problem or a sun does, is a synonym of emerge.

clue.text: Turned on by some form of worship

parts.note: a lamp turned on is lit
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Someone excited by a religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of prayers with responses, a set form of public prayer in church.

clue.text: Take to court about a T-shirt? Injustice!

indicators.note: one word goes about, or around, the others

parts.note: to try someone is to put them on trial
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, a kind of T-shirt

explanation.surface: Suing someone over a T-shirt would be an outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty of justice is a grossly unfair outcome, an injustice.

clue.text: Using a particular method, prepares tomatoes and various items

definitions.text: Using a particular method, prepares tomatoes
definitions.meaning: tomatoes can be preserved by drying them in the sun
odds and ends, miscellaneous small things

explanation.surface: A cook's method for tomatoes, among other bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer describes how sun-dried tomatoes are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are assorted minor articles too small to list separately.

clue.text: Lift woolly to reveal …

indicators.note: something woolly is fuzzy and confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A jumper is pulled up to show what is beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word, and the American word means the same machine.

clue.text: Theatre's promotion: act Shakespeare in an unusually familiar way?

parts.note: to act is to play a part

parts.words: Shakespeare in an unusually familiar way
parts.note: William Shakespeare called by the pet form of his first name is Bill

explanation.surface: A theatre advertises performing Shakespeare in a strikingly casual style.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster advertising a theatre production.

clue.text: … what followed Dior's famous style, they say — most direct approach

indicators.note: says this is a sound-alike, as people pronounce it

parts.note: Dior's A-line was followed by his B-line collection

explanation.surface: Continuing the fashion reveal: the look that came after Dior's famous one.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian Dior launched the A-line in 1955; letter B comes after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a beeline is to head straight for something, like a bee to its hive.

clue.text: Fiery, sailor? Take it easy

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor
to laze is to relax and do nothing

explanation.surface: Someone asks a hot-tempered seaman to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire and burning brightly is fiery.

clue.text: Obama receiving Republican heckle

indicators.note: receiving means taking another letter inside

parts.note: Barack is Obama's first name

explanation.surface: Obama hosts a Republican who jeers at him.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player, a synonym of heckle.

clue.text: Rare blemish on church

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An unusual defect on a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply and seldom found is described as rare.

clue.text: Girl from island accompanied by Frenchman

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from an island goes about with a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's first name, and crosswords often define a name as a girl.

clue.text: Member of clergy facing debts associated with someone else

indicators.note: the vicar faces, or stands in front of, the next piece

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest
IOUs are written promises of money owed

explanation.surface: A clergyman is confronted with what he owes alongside another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious experience is felt through another person rather than directly.

clue.text: See rising study of ancient times

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads the piece upwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Watching a study of old history climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden days are long-past times, so olden means belonging to ancient times.

clue.text: Costumier dated mechanic

parts.note: out of fashion, or simply out, means dated
a fitter assembles and repairs machinery

explanation.surface: A costume maker went out with an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' looks like a verb about romance; it means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both sell or make clothing, so a costumier is a kind of clothes supplier.

clue.text: Car with old sound system

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

explanation.surface: A vintage car fitted with a stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio equipment is gear for reproducing sound, a sound system.

clue.text: Emotional pull found in running

indicators.note: one piece found in another sits inside it

parts.note: tearing means rushing, as in tearing about
a jerk is a sudden pull

explanation.surface: A sudden tug on the feelings felt while racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental film is described as moving the audience to tears, so it is emotional.
